journey.name: TL-16 A failure arriving over a pending undo takes the offer away
journey.description:
KNOWN-DEFECT WATCHLIST. Asserts the current behaviour; whether it is the right behaviour is a product call. See qa/TEST-PLAN.md.
TL-09 shows a second delete overwriting the first undo offer. This is the same single-slot message field reached down the other code path: post() writes TaskDeleted and reportFailure writes Failure into the same nullable field, so any unrelated failure - a toggle, a refresh - that arrives while an undo offer is up silently consumes it.
It matters more than TL-09 because the user did nothing to cause it. One lost dice roll in a background write is enough to take away the only route back from a delete they were still deciding about.
Preconditions: adb shell am force-stop com.rounds.test.to_dolist adb shell am start -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.MainActivity --es qa_failure_rate 0.0

actions.action: Tap the element with the content description "Delete task" on the "Renew domain registration" row
Verify that a message reading "Task deleted" is on screen
Using adb, break the source with `am broadcast -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.qa.QaControlReceiver -a com.rounds.test.to_dolist.QA_SET_FAILURE_RATE --es qa_failure_rate 1.0`
Tap the checkbox with the content description "Mark complete" on the "Reply to design feedback" row
Verify that "No connection. Check your network and try again." is on screen
Verify that no message reading "Task deleted" and no "Undo" action are on screen
Verify that "Renew domain registration" is not on screen and is offered no further way back
Verify that the "Reply to design feedback" row still has an unchecked checkbox
